rule: the spec froze a CONTINGENT device rule decided by a mechanical A/B that looks at no outcome. This record applies that rule. Nothing in the spec is edited.

THE_AB.procedure: experiments/diagnose_compression_student_episode_length.py run once with --device cpu and once with --device cuda on the SAME 8 non-sealed seeds (11930001..11930008), same frozen offline-TD student, forced z0, Pole A, deterministic actions
THE_AB.episodes_differing: 8 of 8 differ in (blue, red); 1 of 8 differs in step count

DECISION_APPLIED_MECHANICALLY.why: the frozen rule: if ANY episode differs across devices, the sealed eval runs on cuda for strict comparability with COMPRESSION_CROSSOVER_EVAL_RESULT.json (which ran on cuda). The simulation's trajectories are device-dependent in floating point, so cpu would have changed the measurement instrument, not just its speed.
DECISION_APPLIED_MECHANICALLY.cost_accepted: ~3.3x slower per episode (29.2 s vs 8.9 s); ~2 h for the 256-episode seal, as observed for the offline-TD seal

KNOWN_CAVEAT_RECORDED_NOT_HIDDEN.collection_vs_eval_device: student-state collection (and the original teacher-state collection) run on cpu per the spec; the sealed evals run on cuda. Because trajectories are device-dependent, the collected deployment states are drawn from a numerically slightly different trajectory distribution than the one the seal scores. This was already true of round 0 (teacher states on cpu, seal on cuda). It is a property of the simulator, is the same for every arm in this program, and is disclosed here rather than corrected mid-protocol.
KNOWN_CAVEAT_RECORDED_NOT_HIDDEN.operational_note_for_future_specs: for this single-env one-episode-at-a-time pattern, cpu is ~3.3x faster than cuda AND numerically different from it; future evaluators should freeze a device up front and keep it fixed across every arm they intend to compare
